html:
The Guadalcanal campaign was fought from 7 August 1942 to 9 February 1943 on and around Guadalcanal in the Solomon Islands. American forces took the island from Japan and held it. It was the first Allied land offensive of the Pacific War.

Japan was building an airfield on Guadalcanal that would threaten the sea route between the United States and Australia. Two months after Midway, US Marines landed, took the airfield and named it Henderson Field. Japan fought for six months to get it back. Its ships brought in troops and supplies at night, and its soldiers attacked the airfield again and again. So many ships sank in the naval battles nearby that the water was called Ironbottom Sound. After the sea fights of November, Japan could no longer supply its men. In February it took off the 10,000 who were left.

Japan lost over 19,000 soldiers, most from hunger and disease. About 7,100 Americans died. Each side lost dozens of ships and over 600 aircraft, losses the United States could replace and Japan could not. From then on Japan was on the defensive. In April 1943 fighters from Henderson Field shot down Admiral Yamamoto; see Operation Vengeance.
